description: The US Environmental Protection Agency publishes an Intelligent Dasymetric Mapping toolbox for ArcGIS Pro. It reallocates population totals from polygons to raster cells using representative densities for land-cover classes, with optional exclusion of uninhabited areas. Inputs determine the geographic extent, reference year and output resolution; the documentation includes a Delaware example using 2010 census blocks and 2011 land cover. Outputs include population-density GeoTIFFs and diagnostic tables. GitHub provides the source and installation instructions under MIT, free of charge. The older Zenodo snapshot labels its licence only as other-open. Running the toolbox requires separately licensed ArcGIS Pro and Spatial Analyst or 3D Analyst. Estimated density is not a direct observation of each household, and classification assumptions limit local accuracy. The tool can prepare population exposure or service-demand inputs for infrastructure simulations. It complements EPA’s open-source GIS implementation with an ArcGIS interface; execution was not tested.
